title: You’re in the crowd…
paragraphs:
You’re in the crowd…
but your heart is still on fire with something you can’t explain.

You look like everyone else.
You sound like everyone else.

But deep inside…
you know something is missing.

That man in the image… staring through smoke and fire…
he’s not just looking at you.
He’s searching.

And maybe—
you feel like he’s searching for you.
Because here’s the truth we don’t say out loud:

You can stand near the fire of God…
and still be cold inside.

You can be around believers…
and still not belong to Christ.

You can say “Lord, Lord”…
and still live like He’s not King.

Jesus warned this in Matthew 7:21—
not everyone who says “Lord” will enter the kingdom,
but the one who does the will of the Father.
Read that again.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Some of us didn’t walk away from God…

We just learned how to stay close enough
to look faithful—
but far enough
to stay in control.

Silent compromise.
Delayed obedience.
Private sin we keep justifying.
And we call it “grace.”
But it’s not grace.
It’s avoidance.
Let me ask you something…
When was the last time your obedience actually cost you something?

When was the last time you said “yes” to God…
and it hurt your pride, your plans, or your comfort?

Or have you built a version of Christianity
that never confronts you?
Because this is the line most people won’t cross:

You don’t belong to the true Church
just because you attend one.
That’s the part religion won’t tell you.

In Acts 2:38, Peter didn’t invite people to join a system.
He said, “Repent… and be baptized… in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins.”
Repent.

That word means turn.
Not adjust. Not explain. Not delay.
Turn.
AHA REVELATION:

The true Church isn’t who gathers…
it’s who has surrendered.
And here’s the mirror you can’t avoid:

If Jesus isn’t Lord over your private life,
He’s not Lord at all.
But don’t miss this…
This is not where the story ends.

Because the same Jesus who confronts you—
also came to save you.

Romans 5:8 says
“While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not when you fixed yourself.
Not when you became worthy.
While you were still hiding.
That fire behind him?
It’s not just destruction.
It’s purification.

Because God doesn’t expose your sin to shame you—
He exposes it to heal you.

Some scholars interpret the “church” (ekklesia) as
“the called-out ones.”

Called out of darkness.
Called out of pretending.
Called out of double lives.
And maybe that’s you right now.

Tired of performing.
Tired of hiding.
Tired of knowing the truth… but not living it.
Here’s the Gospel, clear and unfiltered:

You are a sinner.
Not misunderstood. Not “just struggling.”
Lost.

But Jesus Christ—
the Son of God—lived the life you couldn’t live…
died the death you deserved…
and rose again to give you new life.
Not improved.
New.
Grace is not permission to stay the same.
Grace is the power to become someone new.

2 Corinthians 5:17 says,
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation…”
Not a better version of the old you.
A new creation.
So here’s the invitation.

Not to religion.
Not to routine.
To Jesus.
Repent.

Turn from sin.
Surrender your life.
Follow Him—not halfway, not someday.
Now.
You were not created to blend into the crowd.
You were called out.
Chosen.
Set apart.

And if something in you is shaking right now…
that’s not emotion.
That’s conviction.
And conviction is not rejection.
It’s God calling you home.

not for information, but transformation.
Real discipleship. Real surrender. Real Jesus.
Stay hungry.
You’ll need it again.
And send this to someone who’s close… but not surrendered.
And the next message might be the one you’ve been avoiding.
